title: HealthReach Indonesia: Capacity-Stratified Healthcare Accessibility Under Flood Disruption in South Kalimantan
description:
Independent replication and extension of a disaster-aware geographic healthcare accessibility methodology (Macharia et al., Kenya, 2025 preprint), applied to the January 2021 South Kalimantan, Indonesia floods. Extends the methodology with (1) a district-level healthcare workforce capacity index used to stratify accessibility results, and (2) event-specific disruption modeling from Sentinel-1 SAR-observed flood extent, compared directly against a static BNPB hazard-risk proxy under matched conditions.

Reports two findings and one retraction, in order of confidence: chronic pre-disaster inequality between low- and high-capacity districts (72.8% vs. 90.0% access within 60 minutes); disaster amplification of that gap under real flood disruption (+2.4pp, robust across a matched-penalty sweep and leave-one-district-out check, though a hazard-risk proxy systematically overstates the widening by 1.7-2.6x); and a withdrawn "network-topology chokepoint" mechanism that did not survive a randomization null-model test and is reported as a retraction rather than reframed.

This deposit archives the manuscript (docs/manuscript.md), full pipeline code (src/), six executed analysis notebooks (notebooks/), and the small citable result tables (data/processed/). Large raw geospatial downloads are not included; see README.md for exact reproduction steps and source URLs.
